text: So this guy comes up to me, a little guy, very nervous, and he goes, oh, Mister Trump, Mister Trump, please, please, can I have a picture? Can I have a picture with you? And I said, sure, of course. And he says, oh, thank you, thank you so much, my wife is never going to believe this! Oh my goodness! And his voice was going higher and higher, like this, oh, Mister Trump, you're my hero! I thought he was going to faint. Very nice guy. Very nice. But a very high voice. Later I found out he sings opera. Soprano. Makes sense, actually. Beautiful voice. Very, very high.

And I said to them, you want the best? You want the very best? Then you came to the right place! Because we don't do small, we don't do average, we do tremendous! We do spectacular! When we build something, the whole world stops and looks. They say, how did they do that? How is that possible? And I tell them, it's possible because we dream big, we work hard, and we never, ever quit! Never! So get ready, folks, because what's coming next is going to be the biggest, the best, the most beautiful thing you've ever seen! Are you ready? I said, are you ready? Because here it comes! Here it comes, folks!

Okay. They gave me this paper, and they said I have to read it, so I'm going to read it. The terms and conditions of the golf club membership. Section one. Members must wear collared shirts at all times. Section two. Members must replace all divots on the fairway. Section three. Carts must remain on the cart path near the greens. Section four. No outside food or beverages. Okay. Very exciting stuff. Section five. Guests must be accompanied by a member. That's it. That's the paper. I read it. Can I go now? Section six. No running on the greens. Section seven. Members must pay their dues on time. Okay. That's really it this time.

Ladies and gentlemen, the moment you've all been waiting for. The winner of this year's club championship, the best golfer at this club, the man with the most beautiful swing anybody has ever seen, is me! That's right. Me again. And I want to thank the committee, a very fair committee, very honest people. Some of them work for me, but they're very fair. And I want to thank my caddie, who I beat this time. Not last time. This time. Thank you all very much. It's been a great year, a great year for golf, and a great year for me. Thank you. Thank you so much.

So they asked me, very serious interview, they said, sir, is it true that you're the greatest golfer in the history of this club? Yes. Next question. They said, sir, is it true that you've never lost a match? Next question. Then they said, sir, is it true you lost to your caddie last week? I don't know where you get your information. Very bad information. Terrible sources. Okay, it's true. But he's a very good caddie. One of the best. Next question, please. Then they said, sir, will you ever play your caddie again? Absolutely not. Next question. They said, sir, is it true you hired the caddie to write down your scores? No comment.

Oh, give me a burger, a beautiful burger, with ketchup and pickles and cheese. A tremendous burger, the greatest burger, as golden as golden can be. Oh, the fries are so crispy, the Coke is so cold, it's the finest of meals ever made. And nobody, nobody, makes burgers like me, they're the best that you've ever had. So sing it with me now, everybody sing, a burger, a beautiful thing! The best burger in the world, believe me, folks, the best. A burger, a beautiful thing! Oh, a burger, a burger, the pride of the land, the most beautiful burger in town. La la la, a beautiful thing.

Thank you! Thank you! What a crowd! What a crowd! Look at this, the place is packed, they couldn't even fit everybody inside! There are thousands of people outside! Thousands! Can you hear me in the back? Can you hear me? We are going to win so much, you're going to get tired of winning! You're going to say, please, please, no more winning! And I'm going to say, no! We're going to keep winning! We're going to win and win and win! Are you ready? Are you ready? Let's go! Louder! I can't hear you! Louder! That's what I'm talking about! Thank you, everybody!

Come here, come closer. I'm going to tell you a secret, but you can't tell anybody. Okay? Nobody. You know the chocolate cake at the club? The big one, the beautiful one? Everybody thinks it's a secret family recipe. Very old recipe, very famous. It's not. It's from a box. A regular box from the store. Don't tell anybody. If this gets out, it's over. The members would go crazy. So this stays between us. Just you and me. Okay? Good. Now go have a piece. It's delicious. And don't tell the chef I told you. He's very sensitive. Very sensitive guy. Shh. Okay, go. Go now, before somebody sees us.

Thank you, thank you very much. It's a great honor to be here tonight, a very great honor. Ahem. Excuse me. The air in this room, it's very dry. They have the air conditioning on so high, it's like the North Pole in here. Ahem, ahem. Excuse me. Can somebody get me some water? A little water. Thank you. That's much better. Where was I? Oh, yes, the honor. It's a great honor. Ahem. And we're going to fix that air conditioning, believe me. First thing tomorrow. It's going to be the best air conditioning you've ever felt. Thank you all for being so patient. You're very patient people.

So my friend tells me he's going to beat me at golf. He says he's been practicing for six months, he got a new coach, new clubs, new shoes, everything. Haha. I said, that's great, that's wonderful. First hole, he swings, and the ball goes straight into the woods. Hahaha. Second hole, into the lake! Third hole, he hits a tree, and the ball comes right back at him! Haha, I couldn't stop laughing. I said, how much did you pay that coach? He said, a lot. I said, hehe, ask for your money back. He never played golf with me again. Haha. Smart man.

So this big, tough guy comes up to me, a truck driver, arms like tree trunks, never cried in his life. And he says, sir, Boohoo, sir, I just want to say thank you. Thank you for the golf course. My son got married there last week, and it was the most beautiful day of my life. Sob. And I said, don't cry, don't cry, you're going to make me cry. And he kept going. Boohoo. Big strong guy! Crying like a baby. It was beautiful, actually. Very beautiful. I'll never forget it. His wife was crying, his son was crying, I was almost crying. Almost. I'm very tough.

So I'm driving the golf cart down the big hill on the fourteenth hole, beautiful day, and I press the brake, and nothing happens. Nothing! The cart is going faster and faster, and there's a lake at the bottom of the hill, a big lake. Aaah! I'm turning the wheel, I'm pressing the brake, the caddie is holding on for dear life. Aaaah! And at the last second, the very last second, I turn hard, we spin around, and we stop, one foot from the water. One foot! The caddie looked at me, I looked at him, and I said, we're going to need a new cart. Beautiful cart, too. Very expensive.

Oh, this Diet Coke is so good. So cold. I have a lot of them, a lot, maybe twelve a day, maybe more, I don't count. People say that's too many. I say, it's diet, no calories, it's practically water. Burp. Oh, excuse me. Excuse me. That's the bubbles. The bubbles are very strong in this one. Very powerful bubbles. Burp. Excuse me again. Okay, that's it, I'm done. That was very unpresidential. Very unpresidential. We'll cut that out, right? We'll cut that part. Nobody saw anything. Very powerful bubbles, though. You know, they say you shouldn't drink it so fast. But it tastes much better fast.

Hmm, hmm, hmm. Oh, hello, I didn't see you there. I was just humming a little tune. I always hum when I'm on the putting green, it relaxes me. Very relaxing. Mmm, mmm. My golf coach says it's bad, he says it makes me lose focus. I said, how can it be bad? Look, the ball goes in every time. Well, almost every time. Hmm, hmm. See? Right in the cup. Beautiful. The humming works, believe me. Everybody should hum. It's good for the soul, and it's great for your putting. Hmm, hmm, hmm. Okay, next hole. I'll hum all the way there.

So they give me the new schedule for tomorrow. Six in the morning, breakfast meeting. Seven, another meeting. Eight, phone calls. Nine, more meetings. Uh. Ten, a lunch meeting, at ten in the morning. Who has lunch at ten in the morning? Ahh. And then golf, they say, maybe, if there's time. If there's time! There's never time. I love my job, I really do, I love it, but sometimes, Ahh, sometimes you just want to sit down and have a cheeseburger. That's all. Just one cheeseburger, in peace. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe the day after tomorrow. We'll see. They'll probably add another meeting. Uh. Okay. Let's go to the meeting.

Thank you very much. Sff. Excuse me. It's the allergies, this time of year, all the flowers, everything is blooming. Sff. People always say, why do you sniff so much? I don't sniff! I have perfect breathing, the best breathing. It's the microphone, it's a bad microphone, they gave me a bad microphone. Sff. See? That was the microphone. Very bad microphone. Somebody should look into this microphone. Anyway, where was I? Oh yes, the flowers. Beautiful flowers. Sff. Too many flowers, frankly. Somebody has to talk to the flowers. Next time, I'm going to ask for a better microphone and a lot fewer flowers.
